Package fr.upsaclay.bibs.pacman.model.maze

Class MazeImpl

java.lang.Object
fr.upsaclay.bibs.pacman.model.maze.MazeImpl
All Implemented Interfaces:
Maze
public final class MazeImpl extends Object implements Maze
Concrete implementation of Maze.

Why a separate MazeImpl file?

The project provides Maze as an interface used by tests and by the rest of the application. Keeping the interface separated from its implementation has several benefits:
  • Encapsulation: the internal representation (here a 2D Tile array) stays private and can evolve without breaking the public API.
  • Test compatibility: tests depend on the interface contract, not on a specific implementation.
  • Maintainability: Maze-related logic (bounds checks, wrapping, pixel→tile conversion) is centralized in one concrete class.

This implementation models the maze as a rectangular grid of tiles. Each tile corresponds to a fixed number of pixels (see constants in Maze). Positions of actors are expressed in pixels, but interactions with the maze are tile-based. Therefore the class provides helpers to convert pixels to tile positions and to navigate between tiles.

    • getNeighbourTilePosition

      public TilePosition getNeighbourTilePosition(int line, int col, Direction dir)
      Computes the neighbouring tile position when moving one tile in the given direction. Uses wrap-around (modulo) so going out of the grid re-enters on the other side.

      Why: the original Pac-Man maze has tunnel behaviour; using wrap-around is a simple step-1 behavior that can be refined later if needed (e.g. horizontal-only tunnels).

      Specified by:
      getNeighbourTilePosition in interface Maze
      Parameters:
      line - , the line number
      col - , the col number
      dir - , the direction
      Returns:
      the corresponding tile
